title: Tanvi, Ashmita, Rakshitha storm into Korea Masters quarterfinals
indian_angle: Three Indian women's singles players, Tanvi Sharma, Ashmita Chaliha, and Rakshitha Sree Ramraj, have advanced to the quarterfinals of the Korea Masters.
summary: Indian shuttlers Tanvi Sharma, Ashmita Chaliha, and Rakshitha Sree Ramraj have all secured spots in the Korea Masters 2026 quarterfinals, with Ashmita notably defeating South Korea’s Kim Min Ji.

title: Satwiksairaj Rankireddy's shoulder cleared, coach cautious for World Championships
indian_angle: This news provides an update on the fitness of star Indian doubles player Satwiksairaj Rankireddy ahead of the BWF World Championships, which India is hosting.
summary: Star Indian doubles player Satwiksairaj Rankireddy has received a green light on his shoulder injury after rehab, but his coach remains cautious about his readiness for the upcoming BWF World Championships in New Delhi.

title: Ayush Shetty to face defending champion Shi Yuqi in World Championships opener
indian_angle: Young Indian shuttler Ayush Shetty faces a tough challenge against defending champion Shi Yuqi in his opening match at the BWF World Championships hosted in India.
summary: Indian shuttler Ayush Shetty has been drawn against defending champion Shi Yuqi in the first round of the BWF World Championships, which also sees Lakshya Sen and PV Sindhu having their initial opponents confirmed.

title: Sindhu, Lakshya, Satwik-Chirag: India's medal hopes at home World Championships
indian_angle: This article analyzes the medal prospects of key Indian players like PV Sindhu, Lakshya Sen, and Satwiksairaj Rankireddy-Chirag Shetty at the upcoming BWF World Championships, hosted by India.
summary: With India hosting the BWF World Championships, an analysis delves into the medal prospects of top Indian shuttlers including PV Sindhu, Lakshya Sen, and the men's doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty.

title: BWF satisfied with New Delhi's World Championships venue preparations
indian_angle: The BWF has expressed satisfaction with the preparations of the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, the venue for the BWF World Championships, which India is hosting for the first time in 17 years.
summary: The Badminton World Federation (BWF) has given a positive assessment of the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, the venue for the upcoming World Championships in New Delhi, addressing past operational concerns.

title: BAI implements 3x15 scoring system for domestic junior tournaments
indian_angle: The Badminton Association of India (BAI) has introduced the 3x15 scoring system for U-13, U-15, and U-17 domestic ranking tournaments and national championships.
summary: The Badminton Association of India has announced the implementation of the 3x15 scoring system for U-13, U-15, and U-17 age groups in domestic ranking tournaments and national championships.
